questions.question:
A vector 
a is turned without a change in its length

through a small angle dθ. What are | |a and ∆a?
questions.answer: Magnitude |a| remains unchanged. The change in vector is |Δa| = √(a² + a² - 2a²cos(dθ)) = 2a sin(dθ/2).

questions.question:
Does the speedometer of a car measure speed or
velocity ? Explain
questions.answer: The speedometer measures instantaneous speed only, as it indicates the magnitude of velocity without specifying the direction of motion.
questions.solution: The speedometer measures instantaneous speed only, as it indicates the magnitude of velocity without specifying the direction of motion.

questions.question:
When a particle moves with constant velocity, its
average velocity and its instantaneous velocity & speed
are equal. Comment on this statement.
questions.answer: True. When a particle moves with constant velocity, both its speed and direction remain unchanged. Therefore, its instantaneous velocity, average velocity, and instantaneous speed are all equal.
questions.solution: True. When a particle moves with constant velocity, both its speed and direction remain unchanged. Therefore, its instantaneous velocity, average velocity, and instantaneous speed are all equal.

questions.question:
In a given time interval, is the total displacement
of a particle equal to the product of the average
velocity and the time interval, even when the velocity
is not constant? Explain.
questions.answer: Yes. By definition, average velocity is V_avg = Δr / Δt. Therefore, the total displacement Δr = V_avg · Δt holds universally, even if the velocity varies during the interval.

questions.question:
Can you have zero displacement and a non zero
average velocity? Can you have a zero displacement
and a non zero velocity? Illustrate your answer on a
x-t graph.
questions.answer:
(a) No, zero displacement means V_avg = Δr / Δt = 0. A non-zero average velocity is impossible with zero displacement.
(b) Yes, instantaneous velocity can be non-zero at intermediate instants even if net displacement is zero (e.g. a particle returning to its starting point).

questions.question:
At which point on its path a projectile has the
smallest speed?
questions.answer: At the highest point (peak) of its trajectory, where the vertical velocity component is zero (vy = 0) and the speed equals horizontal velocity u cosθ.
questions.solution: At the highest point (peak) of its trajectory, where the vertical velocity component is zero (vy = 0) and the speed equals horizontal velocity u cosθ.

questions.question:
A person standing on the edge of a cliff at some
height above the ground below throws one ball straight
up with initial speed u and then throws another ball
straight down with the same initial speed. Which ball,
if either, has the larger speed when it hits the ground?
Neglect air resistance.
questions.answer: Both balls hit the ground with the exact same speed. By conservation of mechanical energy: v² = u² + 2gh, which depends solely on initial speed u and height h, irrespective of initial projection angle.
questions.solution: Both balls hit the ground with the exact same speed. By conservation of mechanical energy: v² = u² + 2gh, which depends solely on initial speed u and height h, irrespective of initial projection angle.

questions.question:
An airplane on floor relief mission has to drop a
sack of rice exactly in the center of a circle on the
ground while flying at a predetermined height and
speed. What is so difficult about that? Why doesn’t it
just drop the sack when it is directly above the circle.
questions.answer: Due to inertia, the dropped sack retains the airplane's horizontal velocity and moves in a parabolic trajectory. If dropped directly above the target, it overshoots and lands ahead of the circle.

questions.question:
One of the following statements is incorrect.
(a) The car traveled around the track at a constant
velocity
(b) The car traveled around the track at a constant
speed. Which statement is incorrect and why ?
questions.answer: Statement (a) is incorrect. A car traveling around a curved track cannot have constant velocity because its direction of motion is continuously changing (velocity is a vector). Statement (b) is correct since speed is a scalar and can remain uniform.
questions.solution: Statement (a) is incorrect. A car traveling around a curved track cannot have constant velocity because its direction of motion is continuously changing (velocity is a vector). Statement (b) is correct since speed is a scalar and can remain uniform.

questions.question:
Give an example from your own experience in which
the velocity of an object is zero for just an instant of
time, but its acceleration is not zero.
questions.answer: A ball thrown vertically upward: at the apex of its trajectory, its instantaneous velocity is zero (v = 0), but its acceleration is non-zero (a = g = 9.8 m/s² downward).
questions.solution: A ball thrown vertically upward: at the apex of its trajectory, its instantaneous velocity is zero (v = 0), but its acceleration is non-zero (a = g = 9.8 m/s² downward).

questions.question:
A ball is dropped from rest from the top of a building
and strikes the ground with a speed vf. From ground
level, a second ball is thrown straight upward at the
same instant that the first ball is dropped. The initial
speed of the second ball is v0 = vf, the same speed
with which the first ball will eventually strike the ground.
Ignoring air resistance, decide whether the balls cross
paths at half the height of the building above the
halfway point, or below the halfway point. Give your
reasoning.
questions.answer: The balls cross paths ABOVE the halfway point (at height 3H/4). Since h1 + h2 = H = vf · t, we find t = √(H / 2g). The distance fallen by the first ball is h1 = (1/2)gt² = H/4, meaning the encounter occurs at height H - H/4 = 3H/4 from the ground.

questions.question:
The muzzle velocity of a gun is the velocity of the
bullet when it leaves the barrel. The muzzle velocity
of one rifle with a short barrel is greater than the
muzzle velocity of another rifle that has a longer barrel.
In which rifle is the acceleration of the bullet larger?
Explain your reasoning.
questions.answer: The bullet in the short barrel rifle experiences larger acceleration. Using v² = 2as ⇒ a = v² / (2s). With a higher muzzle velocity v and shorter barrel length s, the short barrel bullet has significantly greater acceleration.
questions.solution: The bullet in the short barrel rifle experiences larger acceleration. Using v² = 2as ⇒ a = v² / (2s). With a higher muzzle velocity v and shorter barrel length s, the short barrel bullet has significantly greater acceleration.

questions.question:
On a riverboat cruise, a plastic bottle is accidentally
dropped overboard. A passenger on the boat estimate
that the boat pulls ahead of the bottle by 5 meters
each second. Is it possible to conclude that the boat
is moving at 5 m/s with respect to the shore? Account
for your answer.
questions.answer: No. The bottle moves with the river current. The 5 m/s observed is the velocity of the boat relative to the water (bottle), not relative to the shore.
questions.solution: No. The bottle moves with the river current. The 5 m/s observed is the velocity of the boat relative to the water (bottle), not relative to the shore.

questions.question:
A wrench is accidentally dropped from the top of
the mast on a sailboat. Will the wrench hit at the
same place on the deck whether the sailboat is at
rest or moving with a constant velocity? Justify your
answer.
questions.answer: Yes, the wrench hits at the exact same location on the deck. By inertia, the wrench shares the sailboat's horizontal velocity, and in the sailboat's inertial reference frame, its vertical fall is identical whether moving or stationary.
questions.solution: Yes, the wrench hits at the exact same location on the deck. By inertia, the wrench shares the sailboat's horizontal velocity, and in the sailboat's inertial reference frame, its vertical fall is identical whether moving or stationary.

questions.question:
Is the acceleration of a projectile equal to zero
when it reaches the top of its trajectory? If not, why
not?
questions.answer: No. Acceleration remains constant at g (9.8 m/s² vertically downward) throughout the entire flight. Only the vertical component of velocity is zero at the peak.
questions.solution: No. Acceleration remains constant at g (9.8 m/s² vertically downward) throughout the entire flight. Only the vertical component of velocity is zero at the peak.

questions.question:
A child is playing on the floor of a recreational
vehicle (RV) as it moves along the highway at a
constant velocity. He has a toy cannon, which shoots
a marble at a fixed angle and speed with respect to
the floor. The connon can be aimed toward the front
or the rear of the RV. Is the range towards the front
the same as, less than, or greater than the range
towards the rear? Answer this question (a) from the
child’s point of view and (b) from the point of view of
an observer standing still on the ground. Justify your
answers.
questions.answer:
(a) In the child's frame of reference (an inertial frame moving with constant velocity), ranges are identical.
(b) In the ground frame: forward range is greater because ground velocity is u cosθ + v_RV, whereas backward range is smaller (u cosθ - v_RV).
questions.solution:
(a) In the child's frame of reference (an inertial frame moving with constant velocity), ranges are identical.
(b) In the ground frame: forward range is greater because ground velocity is u cosθ + v_RV, whereas backward range is smaller (u cosθ - v_RV).

questions.question:
Three swimmers can swim equally fast relative to
the water. They have a race to see who can swim
across a river in the least time. Swimmer A swims
perpendicular to the current and lands on the far shore
downstream, because the current has swept him in
that direction. Swimmer B swims upstream at an angle
to the current and lands on the far shore directly
opposite the starting point. Swimmer C swims
downstream at an angle to the current in an attempt
to take advantage of the current. Who crosses the
river in the least time? Account for your answer.
questions.answer: Swimmer A crosses in the least time. Crossing time depends solely on the velocity component perpendicular to the river bank (t = d / vy). Swimmer A swims directly across, maximizing vy = v_swim (cos 0° = 1), whereas B and C direct part of their velocity along the current, resulting in a smaller vy.
